rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: A landlord ending a tenancy or not renewing a lease must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the notice to quit. The landlord must also send a copy of the notice to the City. A violation does not halt the eviction.
rules.key_value: Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources delivered with every notice to quit or non-renewal; copy filed with the City
rules.quoted_span: The Notice of Tenants’ Rights and Resources must be delivered at the same time as the Notice to Quit.
rules.effective_date_note: The tenant FAQ (D014) states the HSNA becomes effective November 6, 2020. The ordinance was passed in October 2020.
rules.exemptions: Residences in a hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility, and non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.
rules.penalty: 1st offense: warning. 2nd and later offenses: $300 per day, enforced by the Inspectional Services Department.

unverifiable_exemptions: residence in hospital, skilled nursing or health facility
non-profit short-term substance abuse treatment facility

rules.review_note: This is a notice and filing requirement, not a just-cause limit on eviction grounds. Boston has no local limit on eviction grounds in the documents.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb 2017)
rules.requirement: Housing providers with City DND funding or land, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy, may not use a blanket ban on applicants with arrests or convictions. They may not consider non-conviction arrests, convictions with judicial relief, juvenile records, or convictions over 5 years old, and may not use credit scores to approve or deny applications.
rules.key_value: No blanket criminal-history bans; no arrests without conviction, juvenile records, or convictions >5 years old; no credit scores
rules.citation: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy (DND, Feb. 2017)
citation_aliases: Boston Department of Neighborhood Development Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.quoted_span: will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis
rules.effective_date_note: Only the February 2017 policy date is given.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply where a conviction directly relates to the housing sought or poses unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others, or to current criminal behavior. Conflicting federal or state criminal-history requirements preempt it.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies only to housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy.

requires_unknown_facts: property receives DND funding or land, or has income-restricted units under the BPDA Inclusionary Development Policy

rules.review_note: This is a funding-conditioned policy under which providers agree to its terms, not a general ordinance. How it is enforced is unclear.

rules.title: Boston fair housing protections for rental assistance (voucher) holders
rules.requirement: In Boston it is illegal to discriminate in renting based on rental assistance, including Section 8, disability and veterans vouchers. A landlord cannot refuse an applicant because they use a voucher.
rules.key_value: Ban on refusing rental assistance / vouchers
rules.citation: Boston Fair Housing Regulations (Boston Fair Housing Commission)
rules.quoted_span: The landlord tells you they don't accept rental assistance. This includes Section 8 vouchers, social security disability vouchers, and veterans vouchers.
rules.review_note: The page does not give a code section. The citation is inferred from the page title.

no_rule_findings.finding: State law bars municipalities from enacting or enforcing rent control, so Boston has no local rent cap. Home-rule petition H.3744 for Boston rent stabilization was sent to a study order and not enacted.
no_rule_findings.quoted_span: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind

parsed.notes: The Boston documents support only the rules above. They show no city rule on security deposits, application or screening fees, or algorithmic rent setting. Those are governed by state law, so no finding is made for them. Home-rule petition H.3744 (n1) was sent to study. It only shows that no local just-cause eviction law exists beyond the HSNA notice rule, so no separate finding was added.
